title: rootless + runc: PidsLimit 0 still gives pids.max=1 on 6.1.2 (native and Docker-compat API; docker CLI always sends 0)
body:
### Issue Description

On rootless Podman **6.1.2** with the **runc** runtime (cgroup v2, systemd cgroup manager), a PIDs limit of `0` still produces `pids.max = 1`, so the container cannot fork at all. `0` is meant to be "unlimited".

This is the same symptom as #29422, which was closed on 2026-08-07 as working on the latest version. That check most likely ran on crun. On 6.1.2 with runc 1.5.1 it still reproduces, for both the native CLI and the Docker-compatible API.

The Docker-compat path is the one that bites in practice. The **docker CLI 29.8.1 sends `HostConfig.PidsLimit: 0` on every `docker run` that has no `--pids-limit` flag** (Docker's API documents 0 as "no limit"). So with `DOCKER_HOST` pointed at the Podman socket, *every* `docker run` gets `pids.max = 1`, and any image whose entrypoint forks fails: `sh`, `erl`, `rustc` ("OS can't spawn worker thread: Resource temporarily unavailable"), and so on.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Native CLI:

```
$ podman run --rm --pids-limit=0  docker.io/library/alpine:latest cat /sys/fs/cgroup/pids.max
1
$ podman run --rm --pids-limit=-1 docker.io/library/alpine:latest cat /sys/fs/cgroup/pids.max
max
$ podman run --rm                 docker.io/library/alpine:latest cat /sys/fs/cgroup/pids.max
2048
```

Docker-compat API, directly on the socket (`POST /v1.44/containers/create`, then start; `Cmd: ["cat","/sys/fs/cgroup/pids.max"]`), varying only `HostConfig`:

| `HostConfig` | resulting `pids.max` |
|---|---|
| `{}` (PidsLimit omitted) | `2048` |
| `{"PidsLimit": null}` | `2048` |
| `{"PidsLimit": 0}` | **`1`** |
| `{"PidsLimit": -1}` | `max` |

docker CLI (29.8.1, API 1.44) through `DOCKER_HOST=unix:///run/user/1000/podman/podman.sock`:

```
$ docker run --rm alpine cat /sys/fs/cgroup/pids.max
1
$ id=$(docker create alpine true); podman inspect --format '{{.HostConfig.PidsLimit}}' $id
0
$ docker run --rm --pids-limit=-1 alpine cat /sys/fs/cgroup/pids.max
max
```

### Describe the results you received

`PidsLimit` 0 (native `--pids-limit=0`, or compat `HostConfig.PidsLimit: 0`) gives `pids.max = 1`.

### Describe the results you expected

`pids.max = max`, the same as `-1`. That matches Podman's own documentation for `--pids-limit=0` and Docker's API semantics for `PidsLimit: 0`, which the compat endpoint serves.

### podman info output

```
podman 6.1.2 (server API 6.1.2), rootless
OCI runtime: runc 1.5.1 (spec 1.3.0); crun not installed
cgroups: v2, manager systemd
conmon 2.2.1
kernel 7.2.6-arch2-1 (Arch Linux), x86_64
docker CLI 29.8.1 (API 1.44) as the compat client
```

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Rootless

### Upstream Latest Release

Yes

### Additional environment details

containers.conf leaves `pids_limit` at the default (2048).

### Additional information

Workarounds: pass `--pids-limit=-1` explicitly (native or docker CLI), or use `podman run`, which omits the field. Refs #29422.

comments.body:
Reproduced on 6.2.0-dev (rootless, cgroup v2): 
- with default crun, --pids-limit=0 -> pids.max=max; 
- with --runtime=runc, --pids-limit=0 -> pids.max=1.

I am working on a fix.
